title: Linear threshold functions
statement: A Boolean function $f\colon\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ is a linear threshold function if there are real weights $a_1,\ldots,a_n$ and a real threshold offset $a_0$ such that, for every input $x$, its value is the sign of $a_0+\sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i$, with zero assigned the value $1$.
